questions.question: Discuss the causes, effects and management of landslides.
questions.solution_html:
• Definition ((1 mark))
  • A landslide is the downward movement of rock, soil, and debris along a slope under the
  • influence of gravity. It is a common natural hazard in hilly or mountainous regions and can be
  • triggered by natural or human factors.
  • Causes of Landslides( (1 mark))
  • Natural Causes
  • Heavy Rainfall, Earthquakes, Volcanic Activity, Weathering
  • Snowmelt or Rapid Water Flow, SteepSlopes.
  • Human-Induced Causes
  • Deforestation, UnplannedConstruction, Mining and Quarrying, Poor Drainage Systems
  • Overgrazing
  • Effects of Landslides ((2 marks))
  • . Environmental Effects
  •  Destruction of forests, vegetation, and wildlife habitats.
  •  Siltation of rivers and lakes, altering ecosystems.
  •  Increased soil erosion and loss of fertile topsoil.
  • Economic Effects
  •  Damage to infrastructure such as roads, bridges, railways, and buildings.
  •  Loss of agricultural land and decreased productivity.
  •  High costs of rehabilitation and reconstruction.
  • C. Social Effects
  •  Loss of human lives and livestock.
  •  Displacement of communities and homelessness.
  •  Disruption of communication and transportation networks.
  • Management and Mitigation of Landslides
  • Preventive Measures
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain the role of media in reducing panic during evacuation
questions.solution_html:
• Role of Media ( (1 marks))
  • The media plays a crucial role in reducing panic and ensuring orderly evacuation
  • during disasters. By providing accurate, timely, and clear information, it helps people
  • understand the situation and follow safety instructions. Media channels such as
  • television, radio, social media, and newspapers guide the public on safe routes, shelter
  • locations, and emergency contacts.
  • Role of Media in Reducing Panic During Evacuation ( (3 marks))
  • Responsible reporting by media prevents the spread of rumors and misinformation
  • which can create fear and confusion. By broadcasting messages from authorities and
  • experts, media builds trust and confidence among people. In summary, effective
  • communication through media ensures calm behavior, coordinated evacuation, and
  • protection of lives during emergencies.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Differentiate between rebuilding and resilience.
questions.solution_html:
• Definition ((1 mark))
  • Rebuilding refers to the process of reconstructing and restoring damaged
  • infrastructure, housing, and essential services after a disaster. It includes repairing
  • roads, schools, hospitals, and communication systems to restore normal functioning in
  • the community.
  • Resilience means the capacity of individuals, communities, and systems to resist
  • absorb, adapt to, and recover from the effects of disasters quickly and effectively.
  • Building resilience ensures that communities are better prepared to face future
  • hazards and can recover faster with less damage.
  • Difference ((3 marks))
  • Rebuilding
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Summarize hydro-meteorological disasters.
questions.solution_html:
• Definition ( (1 mark))
  • Hydrometeorological disasters are natural hazards caused by water and atmospheric
  • processes. They include events such as floods, cyclones, droughts, storms, and heat
  • waves. These disasters result from extreme weather conditions like heavy rainfall
  • strong winds, temperature variations, or prolonged dry spells.
  • Summary of Hydrometeorological Disasters((3 marks))
  • They can lead to loss of lives, destruction of property, agricultural damage, and
  • disruption of essential services. Effective management involves accurate weather
  • forecasting, early warning systems, disaster preparedness, and community awareness.
  • In short, hydrometeorological disasters are weather-related events that require timely
  • monitoring and preventive measures to reduce their impact on people and the
  • environment.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Briefly explain the basic structure of the Incident Command System
questions.solution_html:
• Basic Structure of the Incident Command System (ICS)
  • Definition ((1 mark))
  • The Incident Command System (ICS) is a standardized organizational structure used for
  • managing emergencies efficiently. It ensures clear communication, coordination, and
  • command during disaster response.
  • The basic structure ((3 marks))
  • Incident Commander (IC)
  • The overall leader responsible for managing the entire operation.
  • Command Staff
  • Public Information Officer – handles media and public communication.
  • Safety Officer – ensures safety of responders.
  • Liaison Officer – coordinates with other agencies.
  • General Staff
  • Operations Section: Executes field response actions.
  • Planning Section: Collects data, prepares action plans.
  • Logistics Section: Provides resources and support.
  • Finance/Administration Section: Manages funds, records, and costs.
questions.final_answer: Finance/Administration Section: Manages funds, records, and costs
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain disaster and its concepts.
questions.solution_html:
• Introduction ((1 mark))
  •  A disaster is a sudden event that causes serious disruption to society, resulting in
  • loss of life, property, and environment.It can be natural (like floods, earthquakes
  • or cyclones) or man-made (like industrial accidents or chemical spills).Disasters
  • affect communities, economies, and the environment, demanding coordinated
  • management and recovery efforts.
  • Definition (any definition)((1 mark))
  • “A disaster is a serious disruption of the functioning of a community or society involving
  • widespread human, material, economic or environmental losses and impacts.”
  • Types of Disasters((2 marks))
  • A. Natural Disasters
  •  Hydrometeorological: Floods, droughts, cyclones, storms.
  •  Geological: Earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, landslides.
  •  Biological: Epidemics, pandemics, pest attacks.
  • B. Man-Made Disasters
  •  Industrial accidents, fires, nuclear leaks, terrorism, deforestation, and pollution.
  • Concepts Related to Disaster((3 mark))
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of using media as a tool for / public education and awareness during disaster planning
questions.solution_html:
• Introduction((2 marks))
  • Media plays a vital role in disaster planning and management by spreading
  • information, educating the public, and promoting preparedness. It includes television
  • radio, newspapers, internet, and social media, which help reach people quickly and
  • effectively before, during, and after disasters.
  • Advantages of Using Media ((4 marks))
  • Quick Dissemination of Information
  • Media spreads early warnings and safety instructions rapidly to a large audience.
  • Public Awareness and Education
  • Helps people understand disaster risks, preparedness steps, and response actions.
  • Behavioral Change
  • Continuous awareness campaigns encourage safer habits and community
  • participation.
  • Transparency and Accountability
  • Keeps government and agencies accountable by reporting on disaster response and
  • relief efforts.
  • Mobilization of Resources
  • Encourages donations, volunteers, and community support for affected people.
  • Two-way Communication (especially through social media)
  • Allows people to share information, seek help, and report emergency needs in real
  • time.
  • Disadvantages of Using Media ((4 marks))
  • Spread of Misinformation or Rumors
  • False or exaggerated news can create panic and confusion among the public.
  • Sensationalism
  • Some media outlets may dramatize events for higher ratings rather than focusing on
  • facts.
  • Unequal Access
  • Rural or remote areas may have limited access to media or internet connectivity.
  • Overload of Information
  • Too much or conflicting information can make it difficult for people to understand
  • real threats.
  • Privacy Issues
  • Excessive media coverage may invade the privacy of victims or affected families.
  • (1x10marks =10)
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

  •  A disaster is a sudden event that causes serious disruption to society, resulting in
  • loss of life, property, and environment.It can be natural (like floods, earthquakes
  • or cyclones) or man-made (like industrial accidents or chemical spills).Disasters
  • affect communities, economies, and the environment, demanding coordinated
  • management and recovery efforts.
  • Definition (any definition)((1 mark))
  • “A disaster is a serious disruption of the functioning of a community or society involving
  • widespread human, material, economic or environmental losses and impacts.”
  • Types of Disasters((2 marks))
  • A. Natural Disasters
  •  Hydrometeorological: Floods, droughts, cyclones, storms.
  •  Geological: Earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, landslides.
  •  Biological: Epidemics, pandemics, pest attacks.
  • B. Man-Made Disasters
  •  Industrial accidents, fires, nuclear leaks, terrorism, deforestation, and pollution.
  • Concepts Related to Disaster((3 mark))

questions.question: Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of using media as a tool for / public education and awareness during disaster planning
questions.solution_html:
• Introduction((2 marks))
  • Media plays a vital role in disaster planning and management by spreading
  • information, educating the public, and promoting preparedness. It includes television
  • radio, newspapers, internet, and social media, which help reach people quickly and
  • effectively before, during, and after disasters.
  • Advantages of Using Media ((4 marks))
  • Quick Dissemination of Information
  • Media spreads early warnings and safety instructions rapidly to a large audience.
  • Public Awareness and Education
  • Helps people understand disaster risks, preparedness steps, and response actions.
  • Behavioral Change
  • Continuous awareness campaigns encourage safer habits and community
  • participation.
  • Transparency and Accountability
  • Keeps government and agencies accountable by reporting on disaster response and
  • relief efforts.
  • Mobilization of Resources
  • Encourages donations, volunteers, and community support for affected people.
  • Two-way Communication (especially through social media)
  • Allows people to share information, seek help, and report emergency needs in real
  • time.
  • Disadvantages of Using Media ((4 marks))
  • Spread of Misinformation or Rumors
  • False or exaggerated news can create panic and confusion among the public.
  • Sensationalism
  • Some media outlets may dramatize events for higher ratings rather than focusing on
  • facts.
  • Unequal Access
  • Rural or remote areas may have limited access to media or internet connectivity.
  • Overload of Information
  • Too much or conflicting information can make it difficult for people to understand
  • real threats.
  • Privacy Issues
  • Excessive media coverage may invade the privacy of victims or affected families.
  • (1x10marks =10)
